newsitem.title: JAPAN: BOJ says has cut outright bond purchases.
newsitem.headline: BOJ says has cut outright bond purchases.

text.p: The Bank of Japan reduced the amount of its outright bond purchases in this morning's operation due to an easing of the year-end fund shortage and a slowdown in bank note growth, a central bank official said on Tuesday.

"Due to a slowdown in bank note growth, the BOJ adjusted the size of its outright bond purchase operation. Also, following an easing of the year-end fund shortage, the BOJ decided it was appropriate to change the size for this operation," the official told Reuters.
The BOJ so far this year has been conducting outright JGB purchase operations twice a month, buying 200 billion yen worth of long-term bonds each time.
This morning, however, the bank offered to buy only 100 billion yen worth of bonds.
